text: What is Sri Lanka's national flower?
funFact: The blue water lily, called Nil Manel, became the national flower in 1986.

text: Which animal is on the Sri Lankan flag?
funFact: The lion on the flag holds a sword and stands for bravery.

text: What is Sri Lanka's national bird?
funFact: The Sri Lanka junglefowl lives only in Sri Lanka and nowhere else in the world.

text: Which ocean is Sri Lanka in?
funFact: Sri Lanka's coastline is about 1,340 km long.

text: Which drink is Sri Lanka famous for growing?
funFact: Tea from Sri Lanka is sold around the world as Ceylon tea.

text: In which month is Sinhala and Tamil New Year?
funFact: Families boil milk until it overflows, a sign of good luck for the year.

text: Which animals live at the Pinnawala orphanage?
funFact: Visitors can watch the elephants bathe in the Maha Oya river.

text: Which is the most popular sport in Sri Lanka?
funFact: Sri Lanka's official national sport is actually volleyball.

text: What colour is a king coconut (thambili)?
funFact: Thambili water is a favourite drink on hot days.

text: Which is the biggest city in Sri Lanka?
funFact: Colombo is Sri Lanka's biggest city and its busiest port.

text: In which city is the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic?
funFact: The Esala Perahera in Kandy parades decorated elephants every year.

text: Which king built the Sigiriya rock fortress?
funFact: Sigiriya's painted frescoes are around 1,500 years old.

text: In which year did Sri Lanka gain independence?
funFact: Independence Day is celebrated every year on 4 February.

text: What is Sri Lanka's highest mountain?
funFact: Pidurutalagala rises to about 2,524 metres near Nuwara Eliya.

text: What is the longest river in Sri Lanka?
funFact: The Mahaweli flows for about 335 km and reaches the sea near Trincomalee.

text: Which city has a fort that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
funFact: Galle Fort was first built by the Portuguese and greatly expanded by the Dutch.

text: What is another name for Adam's Peak?
funFact: Pilgrims climb through the night to watch the sunrise from the top.

text: In which year did Sri Lanka win the Cricket World Cup?
funFact: Sri Lanka beat Australia in the 1996 final in Lahore.

text: Yala National Park is famous for which big cat?
funFact: Yala has one of the highest leopard densities in the world.

text: What are Sri Lanka's official languages?
funFact: English is recognised in the constitution as a link language.

text: Which was the first great royal capital of Sri Lanka?
funFact: Anuradhapura was a royal capital for over a thousand years.

text: Who became the world's first female prime minister in 1960?
funFact: Sirimavo Bandaranaike served as prime minister three times.

text: In which year did Ceylon become the Republic of Sri Lanka?
funFact: The new constitution of 1972 changed the country's name to Sri Lanka.

text: Which was the last kingdom before British rule?
funFact: The Kandyan Kingdom came under British rule in 1815.

text: Which king built the Parakrama Samudra reservoir?
funFact: He is remembered for saying no drop of rain should reach the sea without serving people.

text: Jaffna is the main city of which province?
funFact: Jaffna is famous for the Nallur Kandaswamy temple festival.

text: In which national park is the World's End cliff?
funFact: World's End is a cliff with a drop of about 870 metres.

text: In which ancient city is the Ruwanwelisaya stupa?
funFact: Ruwanwelisaya was built by King Dutugemunu.

text: Kandy is in which province?
funFact: The Central Province hills grow much of the country's tea.

text: What is the Dambulla Cave Temple best known for?
options: Ancient Buddha statues and cave paintings
funFact: The Dambulla Cave Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

text: How many provinces does Sri Lanka have?
funFact: The nine provinces are divided into 25 districts.

text: What is a hopper (appa)?
funFact: Egg hoppers have an egg cooked right in the middle.

text: Which giant sea animals can be seen off Mirissa?
funFact: Blue whales, the biggest animals that have ever lived, swim off Sri Lanka's south coast.

text: What is Sri Lanka's money called?
funFact: Sri Lankan rupee notes show local animals, dancers and landmarks.

text: Which festival fills the streets with lanterns in May?
funFact: Vesak remembers the birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha.

text: What is Sri Lanka's highest waterfall?
funFact: Bambarakanda Falls drops about 263 metres.

text: Which rainforest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
funFact: Sinharaja is home to many plants and animals found nowhere else.

text: The Nine Arches Bridge is near which town?
funFact: The bridge is a famous stop on the hill country railway.

text: Which Sri Lankan bowler took 800 Test wickets?
funFact: Muralitharan is the highest wicket-taker in Test cricket history.

text: Which city has one of the world's largest natural harbours?
funFact: Sailors have used Trincomalee's deep harbour for centuries.

text: In which ancient city are the Gal Vihara rock statues?
funFact: The Gal Vihara Buddha statues were carved into a single granite rock face.

text: In which year did the British take the coastal areas from the Dutch?
funFact: The Dutch had controlled the coast for about 140 years.

text: Which mountain range is part of the UNESCO-listed Central Highlands?
funFact: The Central Highlands were added to the World Heritage list in 2010.

text: Who was the first Sri Lankan to climb Mount Everest?
funFact: She reached the summit of Everest in 2016.

text: Which Olympic medal did Duncan White win in 1948?
funFact: It was Sri Lanka's first Olympic medal, won in the 400 m hurdles.

text: What is Sri Lanka's national tree?
funFact: Young Na leaves are bright red, and the tree's wood is so hard it is called ironwood.

text: How many sides of Sri Lanka touch the sea?
funFact: Sri Lanka is an island, so you can reach the sea from every direction.

text: What is kiribath made from?
funFact: Families eat kiribath on New Year's morning and other special days.

text: Which European country reached Sri Lanka first, in 1505?
funFact: The Portuguese were followed by the Dutch, and later the British.

text: Which is Sri Lanka's largest national park?
funFact: Wilpattu is known for its natural lakes, called villus.

text: What is Sri Lanka's official national sport?
funFact: Many people guess cricket, but volleyball was made the national sport in 1991.

text: Minneriya National Park is famous for which event?
funFact: In the dry season, hundreds of elephants gather around the Minneriya tank.

text: Which city became the royal capital after Anuradhapura?
funFact: Polonnaruwa's ancient city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

text: In which year did Sri Lanka introduce voting for all adults?
funFact: Women could vote from 1931, making Ceylon one of the first colonies in Asia to allow it.

text: Lake Gregory is in which town?
funFact: The lake was created in 1873 under Governor William Gregory.
